title: Transcription: Jack DeJohnette – Directions (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 1 August 2021)
notes: Miles Davis, Live at the Fillmore East. Bars 1-5: eighth-note quintuplets on the snare, the cymbal and bass drum on the first of each group, five in a half note; Bishop: 'he may have worked out the 5s, or maybe he's thinking something else and is just pushing the rhythm around.' The groove: the cymbal with the bass drum, the left hand on the snare, 'non-independent'. Marked 121 under cut time. Post and image read in full.

title: DeJohnette patterns (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer)
notes: Patterns 7 and 19, from his Directions and Climax transcriptions, are 'polyrhythmic/polymetric patterns that can be played over two or more bars of 4/4'. Summary only.

title: Groove o' the day: Jack DeJohnette – Polar AC (Todd Bishop, 26 March 2022)
notes: At 173, straight eighths: a 'mostly-linear snare drum and bass drum' groove under eighths on the cymbal, the snare 'at a pretty even volume'. Read in full.

title: Groove o' the day: Jack DeJohnette – Soft Blue (Todd Bishop, 18 January 2022)
notes: At 157: 'an Elvin-like groove, very repetitively'; 'he virtually never deviates from the exact pattern'; a two-bar groove, rim clicks, a triplet on the low tom. Read in full.

title: Groove o' the day: Jack DeJohnette – On the Nile (Todd Bishop)
notes: Written in 3/4 at 122, 'all dotted quarter notes', swung eighths, triplet pickups on the toms; 'a very Elvin Jones-like mode'. Read in full.

title: Groove o' the day: Jack DeJohnette – Fiesta (Todd Bishop, 13 October 2021)
notes: Half note 130: a samba, the bass drum on 1 and the 'a', a bell figure, the toms answering; 'basically this for most of the body of the tune'. The first image read in full.

title: Transcription: Jack DeJohnette – Gentle Rain (Todd Bishop, 8 August 2022)
notes: At 117: 'one cymbal, rim clicks on the snare drum (sparsely), and bass drum', 'a tresillo-type rhythm on the bass drum'. The image read only approximately.

title: Transcription: Jack DeJohnette – On Green Dolphin St. (Todd Bishop, 28 August 2025)
notes: Lee Konitz, Satori: a duo at 199; the foot off 2 and 4; triplet comping in bars 8, 13-20 and 25-36. Read in full.

title: Groove o' the day: Jack DeJohnette – 47th Groove (Todd Bishop, 13 January 2025)
notes: Special Edition, at 115: two grooves, 'each of these grooves pretty repetitively'; the tempo varies with the sections. Read in full.

title: Transcription: Jack DeJohnette – Timeless (Todd Bishop, 20 September 2018)
notes: Brushes over a vamp of 4/4, 4/4, 6/4; a Paiste 602 flat ride. Read in full.

title: Best books: The Art of Modern Jazz Drumming, DeJohnette and Perry (Todd Bishop, 4 April 2022)
notes: The book's 'meter-within-meter' chapter: 'mostly, playing 3/4 ideas in a 4/4 setting'. The review read; the book not.

title: Decoding the Style of Jack DeJohnette: An Analysis of His Approach to the Drums (James Conran, honours thesis, St. Francis Xavier University, 2024)
notes: Picture 3 (Pictures, ECM, 1977): 'a two-beat phrase; four, three-beat phrases; and then another two-beat phrase' (fig. 1.1); a three-beat ride phrase in the solos on Boo Ann's Grand, Climax and Billie's Bounce, traced to Tony Williams; phrasing that 'does not adhere to the measure as much as Jones does'; 'washing machine time' (Riley, quoted). Text read through a text extraction; the figures not seen.

title: Melodic Expression on the Drum Set: Jack DeJohnette's Contribution to the History of Jazz Drumming (Heidi Burns, honours thesis, St. Francis Xavier University, 2024)
notes: Nardis (Bill Evans at Montreux, 1968), bars 17-24: 'a quarter note triplet figure' on the high tom against the melody's eighths, 'the rhythmic hemiola or three over two ratio' (her transcription). Jacknife's B section 'a ride pattern in three against the 4/4 pulse'. The late Sonor Hilite kit, toms tuned to chords. Eddie Harris; the AACM. Text read through a text extraction; the figures not seen.

title: Jack DeJohnette (Percussive Arts Society Hall of Fame, Rick Mattingly)
notes: Born 9 August 1942, Chicago; piano from four; 'multi-directional music'; 'My style at that time was a mixture of Elvin and Tony'; Charles Lloyd, Bill Evans, Miles Davis, Gateway, Keith Jarrett, Special Edition; Peter Erskine: 'I can't play any Jack licks because he doesn't have any'. Read in full.

title: Jack DeJohnette, dynamic and instantly recognizable jazz drummer, dies at 83 (Nate Chinen, NPR, 27 October 2025)
notes: Died in Kingston, New York; built his time from Roy Haynes and Rashied Ali, spreading the emphasis round the kit, 'earthy and elastic'. Read in full.

title: Jack DeJohnette - Wikipedia
notes: Died 26 October 2025; active 1961-2025; jazz, post-bop, fusion, avant-garde. Read as a summary.

title: Polar AC - Wikipedia
notes: Freddie Hubbard, CTI, 1975; the title track recorded 16 September 1971 with DeJohnette, the other tracks with Lenny White and Billy Cobham.

title: Jack of Clubs: DeJohnette drum clinic at Ronnie's (Mark Gilbert, Jazz Journal, March 1981)
notes: A Sonor Signature set; toms tuned 'to a scale, a major triad, diminished scale, fourths', 8 and 10in toms 'in the bongo range'; 'If you tune your drums up ... you'll come through'. Read in full.
